Job Description:
DePuy Synthes, the orthopedics business of Johnson & Johnson, is recruiting for a North America Transport Operations Lead (M1), preferably based in Raynham, with remote as an alternative location in North America.

Johnson & Johnson announced plans to separate its Orthopedics business to establish a standalone orthopedics company, operating as DePuy Synthes. The process of the planned separation is anticipated to be completed within 18 to 24 months, subject to legal and regulatory requirements. Should you accept this position, it is anticipated that, following conclusion of the transaction, you would be an employee of DePuy Synthes, and your employment would be governed by DePuy Synthes employment processes, programs, policies, and benefit plans.

Purpose of the Position
The North America Transport Operations Lead (M1) is a key member of the global supply chain function, responsible for operational management of the transportation network across the North America region, including importation from global sites in other regions.
The role ensures the reliable, cost-efficient, and fully compliant movement of products — from manufacturing sites and regional hubs into local distribution centers, hospitals, and distributors — while safeguarding adherence to customs and international trade regulations across all operating countries.
This is a single regional leadership position that brings together two closely related disciplines: how products physically move (transportation networks, carriers, logistics providers) and how they cross borders compliantly (customs, import/export, trade documentation). The role partners closely with regional and global stakeholders enable uninterrupted product flow, mitigate risk, and drive continuous improvement.

Key Responsibilities
- Drive value across North America through optimized regional transportation flows for both inbound freight (from manufacturing sites and global hubs to regional hubs, and from hubs to local affiliates and distributor warehouses).

- Manage relationships with third-party and fourth-party logistics providers (including global Control Tower partners) through performance metrics, strategic direction, and continuous improvement programs.

- Support further deployment, development and maturity of the Global control tower in the North America region

- Lead performance measurement of transport reliability through critical metrics aligned with regional Plan, Make, and Deliver operations teams; provide input into executive performance reviews.

- Deliver on annual cost improvement and productivity targets through operational improvements while protecting service, quality, reliability, and compliance.

- Translate regional inventory strategy and business requirements into innovative transportation solutions; support transportation set-up for manufacturing network changes and new product launches.

Cross-Functional Leadership
- Partner with regional and global supply chain, Trade Compliance operations, Quality, finance, and legal teams to enable compliant product movement and rapid issue resolution.

- Represent transportation in end-to-end supply chain forums, projects, and sales and operations planning discussions; drive process alignment and trade-off decisions.

- Actively collaborate with the regional Deliver lead, distribution operations, and demand & supply planning teams to optimize capacity planning, reliability, and adherence to service commitments.

- Support product launches, network changes, and supply chain transformations by assessing and managing transportation impacts.

Key Objectives / Metrics
- Transportation cost and continuous improvement savings delivery.

- Transportation reliability — manufacturing/hub to distribution center, and distribution center to customer.

- Logistics provider (Control Tower) performance against agreed service levels and value creation targets.

Qualifications
Education
- Bachelor's degree required (Supply Chain, Logistics, Business, International Trade, or related field).

- Master's degree or MBA preferred.

Required Experience and Skills
- 6–8 years of progressive experience in supply chain, transportation, trade compliance, logistics, or related operational roles, aligned with a manager-level position.

- Strong working knowledge of international trade, customs regulations, and import/export operations within North America.

- Solid expertise across core transportation, planning, and carrier / logistics-provider management, including familiarity with control-tower operating models.

- Excellent analytical skills and an affinity for numbers: ability to support budgeting, financial reconciliation, and identify cost-saving opportunities in transportation.

- Good understanding of the order-to-cash process and end-to-end supply chain mindset.

- Experience partnering with global stakeholders and operating within a matrixed, multinational organization.

- Proven ability to manage complex operational issues, assess risk, and drive compliant outcomes.

- Effective communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills across cultures and geographies.

Preferred Experience and Skills
- Experience in medical devices, pharmaceuticals, or other highly regulated industries.

- Familiarity with global trade systems, transportation management systems, enterprise resource planning platforms, and transport & trade visibility & automation tools.

- Demonstrated experience leading regional or global process standardization initiatives.

- Understanding of good distribution practice and a quality-first approach.

- Lean or continuous improvement certification is a plus.

- Demonstrated awareness of artificial intelligence concepts and responsible / ethical use, with experience generating effective prompts to boost productivity.

Other
- Language: English required; additional languages are a plus.

- Travel: Up to 25–30% regional and international travel.

Job Description:

Please note that this role is available across multiple countries and may be posted under different requisition numbers to comply with local requirements. While you are welcome to apply to any or all of the postings, we recommend focusing on the specific country(s) that align with your preferred location(s):

Cork, Ireland/ Diegem, Belgium - Requisition Number: R-099284
Zug/Zuchwil, Switzerland - Requisition Number: R-099816

DePuy Synthes is establishing a standalone Orthopaedics company. The process of the planned separation is anticipated to be completed within 18 to 24 months of the original announcement date of October 2025, subject to legal requirements, including consultation with works councils and other employee representative bodies, as may be required, regulatory approvals and other customary conditions and approvals.

Should you accept this position, it is anticipated that, following conclusion of the transaction, you would be an employee of DePuy Synthes, and your employment would be governed by DePuy Synthes employment processes, programs, policies and benefit plans. In that case, details of any planned changes would be provided to you by DePuy Synthes at an appropriate time and subject to any necessary consultation processes.
DePuy Synthes, a ~$9 billion business, has an outstanding opportunity for a Senior Finance Manager operating within Supply Chain Finance to gain extensive exposure across DePuy Synthes Principal Operations while leading the Currency Management team.
Role Overview
In this role, you will provide financial leadership to the Currency Management team, leading the identification and management of foreign currency exposures, centralized hedging, hedge and inventory accounting, forecasting, analytics and reporting across DePuy Synthes.
You will play a critical role in standing up the group to operate as a standalone DePuy Synthes Principal Operations team, ensuring that essential currency management activities continue to be performed to the highest standards of compliance, accuracy and insight before, during and after separation.
The immediate focus of the role will be to stand up the Currency Management team and its operating model; establish the end-to-end exposure identification, hedge submission, accounting and control processes required to support placement of hedges through a third-party provider; and lead the development and ongoing maintenance of replacement calculation and analytics capabilities as existing systems will not be available to DePuy Synthes following separation.

Key Responsibilities
- Lead, coach and develop a global team of three finance professionals.
- Serve as the first point of contact for currency-related topics and questions across DePuy Synthes.
- Lead the identification and management of foreign currency exposures, including centralized forecasting and balance sheet hedging, and establish the process required to place hedges with a third-party provider.
- Ensure accurate and compliant hedge and inventory accounting in line with US GAAP and relevant accounting procedures.
- Lead the calculation, analysis, reporting and communication of actual and forecast transactional currency impacts across DePuy Synthes P&L lines, including driver-based variance analysis, trends, risks and opportunities.
- Provide currency analytics, insights and recommendations to DSPO, FP&A, Treasury and senior management.
- Lead regular currency and hedge-result reviews with business partners and senior leadership and provide training and educational materials to strengthen understanding of currency and hedging principles across DePuy Synthes.
- Lead the design, build, testing and deployment of a replacement tool to support currency calculations, hedging, analytics and reporting, and oversee its ongoing maintenance and enhancement.
- Drive standardized and efficient processes through automation and analytics tools, including Power BI and Alteryx.
- Partner across DSPO, Treasury, Tax, FP&A, Technology and Project Osprey teams to stand up the Currency Management team and ensure continuity of critical activities through separation.

Qualifications and Experience
- Bachelor’s degree is required, preferably with a major in Accounting, Economics or Finance; a Master’s degree, MBA or recognized financial qualification such as ACA, ACCA or CIMA is preferred.
- Minimum of 7 years of finance, accounting or related business experience.
- Demonstrated leadership capability, with the ability to develop others, support organizational health and remove barriers to success.
- Strong analytical skills and proven ability to bring clarity to complex business issues, manage complex projects and processes, and translate complexity into practical solutions.
- Excellent communication and business partnering skills, including the ability to frame complex data, simplify written communications, influence internal customers and work effectively with all management levels.
- Confident presenting to senior management, facilitating discussion and providing clear recommendations and solutions.
- Ability to operate independently in a dynamic, high-visibility global environment, manage competing priorities and collaborate effectively across a virtual matrix organization.
- Strong continuous improvement mindset; Supply Chain experience and proficiency with TMI, Alteryx or Power BI are preferred.
- Demonstrated understanding of AI concepts and frameworks, including awareness of responsible and ethical AI practices, and has experience generating effective prompts to boost efficiency and productivity.

Leadership Capabilities
- Leads and develops talent through coaching, delegation and clear accountability.
- Builds trusted relationships and influences effectively across a global organization.
- Combines strategic thinking with strong execution, prioritization and attention to detail.
- Demonstrates integrity, resilience and a strong continuous improvement mindset.

Our Culture of Inclusion
Our Credo guides our commitment to an inclusive work environment where every person is respected as an individual. We value different abilities, backgrounds, experiences and perspectives, and we want every colleague to belong, thrive and reach their potential.
DePuy Synthes is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment in accordance with applicable law, without discrimination based on any legally protected characteristic.

Budget Management, Detail-Oriented, Financial Analysis, Leadership, Stakeholder Management

Preferred Skills:
Data Quality, Developing Others, Execution Focus, Expense Controls, Financial Forecasting, Financial Reports, Financial Risk Management (FRM), Inclusive Leadership, Internal Controls, Program Management, Risk Management, Sarbanes-Oxley Compliance, Succession Planning, Tactical Planning, Vendor Management

Position Summary
Director, Finance Transformation is a senior technology and transformation leader responsible for shaping and executing the Finance ERP target state roadmap for Johnson & Johnson's Finance SAP S/4HANA ecosystem and enabling  finance transacting process simplification. This role provides end-to-end technology leadership for shaping roadmaps, technology solution,  deployments, and ongoing evolution of core finance transaction process simplification across Invoice-to-Cash (I2C), Procure-to-Pay (P2P), Record-to-Report (R2R), Treasury, Tax, and related finance platforms.
The Director is accountable for translating finance transformation priorities into scalable technology solutions that standardize, simplify, automate, and strengthen financial processes, controls, and data integrity across the enterprise. Leveraging deep expertise in SAP S/4HANA Finance, finance operations, and large-scale ERP transformations, this leader will drive business value through  technology core modernization and innovation while ensuring solutions are secure, compliant, resilient, and aligned with enterprise architecture standards.

Major Duties & Responsibilities

1. Finance S/4 Transformation leadership
- ERP target state - Define and shape the strategic roadmap for the Finance SAP S/4HANA transacting platform, ensuring alignment to enterprise finance transformation priorities, business value, regulatory needs, and technology modernization goals.
- Provide technology leadership on SAP S/4HANA Finance, Central Finance, APM, VIM, Treasury, Tax, I2C, P2P, R2R, and related finance systems.
- Translate finance business strategies into scalable technology capabilities, sequencing transformation work across releases, deployments, integrations, and run-state priorities.
- Identify required investments, capability gaps, dependencies, risks, and value opportunities across the finance technology portfolio.

2. End-to-End Finance Process Design and Simplification
- Lead end-to-end design and integration of finance processes within SAP S/4HANA, ensuring transaction flows, posting logic, master data, controls, and reporting outcomes are designed holistically.
- Drive process simplification, standardization, and reduction of customizations by maximizing SAP standard capabilities and eliminating manual workarounds.
- Ensure finance processes are designed with strong business controls, audit readiness, SOX compliance, data integrity, and operational resilience.
- Partner with Finance process owners to simplify and modernize high-volume transactional processes, for example invoice processing, payment execution, cash application, intercompany, close, reconciliations, and exception management.

3. Finance Transacting Process Simplification and Automation
- Create the roadmap for simplifying, standardizing, and automating core finance transacting processes where there is clear business value, control readiness, and technology feasibility.
- Identify opportunities to reduce manual effort, streamline handoffs, and improve exception management across close, reconciliation, invoice exception handling, cash application, payment matching, forecasting support, and operational issue resolution.
- Partner with AI, data, architecture, security, and governance teams to ensure automation and emerging technology solutions are compliant, explainable, secure, auditable, and aligned with enterprise standards.
- Evaluate and guide the use of SAP-native capabilities, SAP BTP, SAP Business Data Cloud, SAP Datasphere, Microsoft Copilot, intelligent automation, and approved AI tools to enable pragmatic value now and scalable capabilities over time.

4. Program Execution and Delivery Leadership
- Lead execution of the Finance S/4 transformation roadmap across complex global deployments, releases, and integration milestones.
- Own delivery plans, resource needs, dependency management, testing strategy, cutover readiness, risk mitigation, and value realization for capabilities in scope.
- Drive disciplined SDLC execution, solution governance, release management, vendor performance, and program financial accountability.
- Proactively identify blockers, integration risks, capacity constraints, and design decisions requiring escalation, and bring cross-functional teams together to resolve issues.

5. Technology Architecture, Data, and Integration Leadership
- Provide leadership across finance application architecture, integration patterns, data flows, and platform decisions supporting SAP S/4 Finance and connected systems.
- Ensure integrations with boundary systems, treasury platforms, tax engines, procurement solutions, reporting layers, data platforms, and AI-enabled services are secure, resilient, scalable, and fit for enterprise operations.
- Partner with enterprise architecture and cybersecurity teams to guide decisions across SAP BTP, Integration Suite, APIs, data platforms, analytics, cloud infrastructure, and emerging SAP capabilities.
- Ensure technology design enables business continuity, system stability, performance, observability, and long-term supportability.

6. Stakeholder, Talent, and Operating Model Leadership
- Serve as a trusted strategic partner to senior Finance and Technology leaders, translating complex finance process needs into clear technology choices and executable roadmaps.
- Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing team of functional, technical, product, architecture, and delivery professionals.
- Build strong partnerships across global, sector, and regional teams to align priorities, manage interdependencies, and drive adoption of standard finance capabilities.
- Foster a culture of accountability, innovation, inclusion, continuous improvement, and disciplined delivery.

- Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree in Information Technology, Finance, Business, Engineering, or related field preferred.
- 15+ years of experience in global technology, finance process transformation, ERP transformation, or enterprise application leadership roles.
- 10+ years of deep SAP S/4HANA Finance experience, including large-scale implementation, deployment, integration, or platform leadership responsibilities.
- Strong functional understanding of finance transacting processes such as accounting , including Invoice-to-Cash, Procure-to-Pay, Record-to-Report, Treasury, Tax, payments, close, reconciliations, intercompany, and financial controls.
- Proven experience leading SAP S/4 Finance transformation programs, Central Finance, global template deployments, and integration with multiple source ERPs or boundary systems.
- Demonstrated ability to define technology strategy, build roadmaps, manage investment priorities, and execute complex global transformation programs.
- Experience with SAP BTP, SAP Integration Suite, SAP Datasphere, SAP Analytics Cloud, SAP Business Data Cloud, BW/4HANA, cloud platforms, APIs, middleware, or enterprise data platforms preferred. RISE migration experience is a plus
- Strong data skills and Knowledge of AI, GenAI, intelligent automation, agentic workflows, machine learning, or automation use cases in finance strongly preferred.
- 10+ years of people leadership experience, including building, mentoring, and leading high-performing teams in a matrixed global environment.
- Demonstrated experience managing vendors, system integrators, budgets, contracts, delivery quality, and senior stakeholder expectations.
- Strong understanding of SDLC, SOX, GxP where applicable, cybersecurity, data privacy, audit readiness, and IT governance requirements.
- Excellent communication, influencing, executive storytelling, and decision-framing skills, with the ability to engage effectively across Finance, Technology, and senior leadership audiences.

Preferred Competencies
- Strategic thinker with strong execution discipline and the ability to move from vision to measurable outcomes.
- Deep finance and technology fluency, with the ability to challenge both business process design and technical solution decisions.
- Strong systems thinking, with the ability to understand how process, data, control, and integration decisions affect the broader finance landscape.

Job Description:
The Sr Finance Manager CFM IM Americas will lead the CFM and controllership agenda for Innovative Medicine Americas from Bogotá. This highly visible leadership role is accountable for the integrity of actuals, financial reporting excellence, and end-to-end close execution across a complex regional and global portfolio. As the senior authority on actuals, the leader partners with senior Finance stakeholders to drive strong governance, actionable insights, and informed business decisions. The role leads a senior finance organization, mobilizes the broader A2R and GSF network across the Americas, and drives operational excellence, risk mitigation, and the development of a scalable, high-performing finance organization.

Core Accountabilities

- Own controllership of actuals for the assigned portfolio and serve as the lead authority on financial results, ensuring accurate, complete, timely and decision-ready reporting under US GAAP and applicable company policies.
-  Lead the end-to-end close governance, including pre-close readiness, closing calendar execution, trial balance review, income statement and balance sheet reviews, cash flow analysis, risk assessment, financial commentary, BRAVO submissions and final close sign-off or green-light within the defined governance model.
- Translate financial results into clear insights for Finance Directors, CFOs, FP&A and business leaders, explaining key drivers, identifying risks and opportunities, and recommending practical actions that protect financial integrity and improve business outcomes.
- Act as the primary senior Global Services Finance partner for the assigned businesses, building trusted relationships and serving as the right hand to sector and regional Finance leadership on actuals, accounting, controls, reporting and transformation matters.
- Lead through influence across A2R, GSF, FP&A, Business Unit Finance, Tax, Treasury, Compliance, Corporate Services and other process teams to resolve issues, clarify ownership, strengthen handoffs and deliver integrated end-to-end outcomes.
- Establish disciplined risk and issue management, including early identification, materiality assessment, executive communication, root-cause analysis, remediation plans, clear accountability and follow-through to sustainable closure.
- Maintain a strong control environment, ensure SOX compliance and audit readiness, and coordinate timely responses to internal and external audit requests and remediation actions.
- Shape the future-state organization by defining capabilities, governance, ways of working, talent needs and scalable service-delivery practices, while protecting business continuity during transitions.
- Drive simplification, standardization, automation and digital enablement across the portfolio, challenging legacy practices and converting improvement opportunities into implemented, sustainable solutions.
- Lead, coach and develop a high-performing team, setting clear expectations, building technical and leadership capability, strengthening succession pipelines and fostering inclusion, accountability, collaboration and continuous learning.

Scope-Specific Mandate

- Lead an Americas-wide controllership model that provides consistent governance while recognizing market complexity, portfolio dynamics and differences accounting reporting requirements.
- Partner with Innovative Medicine regional and market Finance leaders to understand commercial and economic drivers, loss-of-exclusivity impacts, product and portfolio changes, gross-to-net considerations, operating expense movements and other factors affecting actuals.
- Ensure robust P&L, balance-sheet, cash-flow and risk reviews across the region, connecting market-level issues to regional implications and communicating decision-ready insights to senior leadership.
- Coordinate cross-market accounting positions and recurring or emerging risk areas, driving consistency, documentation, escalation and timely remediation across A2R, GSF, BUF and FP&A.
- Lead the integration of new businesses, reporting structures, systems or scope changes into the CFM operating model, with disciplined transition governance and business continuity.
- Build a strong Americas community of practice, sharing insights and standards across North America and other Americas markets while developing scalable capabilities in Bogotá.

Key Stakeholder Relationships

- Innovative Medicine Americas CFOs, Finance Directors, market Controllers, BUF and FP&A leaders.
- Regional and market A2R and GSF teams, global CFM forums and finance process owners.
- Tax, Treasury, Compliance, Corporate Reporting, Internal Audit and External Audit.
- Commercial, supply-chain and transformation stakeholders when business events affect accounting, controls or reporting.

Leadership and Change Expectations

- Demonstrate executive presence and communicate complex accounting and financial topics with clarity, confidence and appropriate judgment for senior audiences.
- Navigate ambiguity and competing priorities across countries, functions and time zones, making sound decisions while balancing accuracy, speed, risk and stakeholder needs.
- Lead organizational and process change with a structured, people-centered approach, helping teams and stakeholders understand the case for change, adopt new ways of working and sustain performance through transition.
- Create an environment where team members understand the business, connect their work to enterprise outcomes, raise risks early and contribute ideas that improve the operating model.
- Model integrity, accountability, inclusive leadership and constructive challenge, reinforcing a culture where issues are surfaced transparently and resolved collaboratively.
- Support the evolution from a primarily CFM-focused model toward integrated CFM and Legal Entity controllership, bringing together management reporting, statutory and legal-entity perspectives where the future operating model requires it.
- Help define the governance, role clarity, capability plan and transition roadmap required to integrate Legal Entity Controller responsibilities without weakening core CFM ownership of actuals or business partnership.

Qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Economics, Business Administration or a related field required; postgraduate degree or MBA preferred.
- CPA, CMA or equivalent professional accounting qualification preferred.
- Minimum 10 years of progressive finance experience, with significant depth in controllership, accounting, external or management reporting, financial analysis and complex matrix organizations.
- At least 5 years of people-leadership experience, including demonstrated success developing managers and/or senior individual contributors and building high-performing teams.
- Strong knowledge of US GAAP required; practical exposure to IFRS and/or local GAAP, statutory reporting, tax coordination and legal-entity accounting strongly preferred.
- Demonstrated experience supporting North American markets or senior North American stakeholders strongly preferred.
- English proficiency at C1 level or equivalent, with the ability to lead executive meetings, negotiations and presentations and to produce clear, nuanced written communication.
- Experience with SAP and enterprise financial reporting environments; and exposure to CFIN, BRAVO, TM1/EPM, BlackLine/Cadency, Power BI, Alteryx, UiPath or similar tools is an advantage.
- Availability to collaborate across North American and global time zones and to travel domestically or internationally as business needs require.

Critical Capabilities

- Controllership and technical accounting depth
- Executive business partnering and stakeholder influence
- Strategic thinking and organization shaping
- Risk identification, judgment and decisive issue resolution
- Financial storytelling and executive communication
- People leadership, coaching and succession development
- Cross-functional and cross-cultural leadership through influence
- Transformation, change leadership and operating-model design
- Process standardization, digital fluency and continuous improvement
- Business acumen, intellectual curiosity and learning agility

Preferred Experience for This Portfolio

- Experience supporting pharmaceutical or Innovative Medicine businesses and complex regional portfolios.
- Demonstrated experience managing multiple markets, preferably including the United States, Canada and/or broader Americas.
- Understanding of revenue reserves, gross-to-net, inventory, intercompany, foreign exchange and market-specific accounting or statutory considerations is highly valued.

Success Profile

The successful candidate will combine the rigor of a controller, the perspective of a strategic finance partner and the leadership of an organization builder. This leader will be equally comfortable challenging an accounting conclusion, guiding a CFO through risks and opportunities, mobilizing multiple execution teams, developing talent and shaping a scalable future-state model from Bogotá.

Job Overview
The Finance Manager, Transformation Office serves as a strategic finance partner to business and transformation leaders, providing financial leadership, performance insights, and decision support to accelerate business performance and transformation outcomes.
Reporting into the Director, Transformation within the DS International Business Controlling team, this role is responsible for leading financial planning, business case development, value realization tracking, and performance management across key transformation initiatives. The Finance Manager will influence senior stakeholders across Finance, Commercial, Supply Chain, Operations, and Program Management teams, ensuring transformation investments deliver sustainable business value.

Transformation Execution & Governance
- Lead the day-to-day execution of strategic transformation initiatives across International Controlling, ensuring alignment with transformation objectives, timelines, and expected outcomes.
- Support the development and maintenance of transformation roadmaps, workplans, milestones, and success metrics.
- Establish robust tracking mechanisms to monitor progress, risks, dependencies, and benefit realization across transformation initiatives.

- Ensure accurate and timely reporting of transformation progress and impact.

- Lead project workstreams and coordinate activities across cross-functional teams.
- Coach, mentor, and provide guidance to analysts and project team members.
- Foster a high-performance environment focused on accountability, execution excellence, and continuous improvement.

- Support audit readiness and documentation requirements associated with transformation initiatives.

- CPA, CMA, ACCA, CIMA, or equivalent professional certification.

- Experience leading financial planning, forecasting, and performance management processes.
- Strong experience developing business cases, financial models, and investment analyses.
- Proven ability to drive cross-functional initiatives and manage multiple complex priorities.

Preferred:
- Experience supporting large-scale transformation, separation, integration, or business improvement programs.
- Experience in a multinational and matrixed environment.
- Knowledge of value realization and program governance frameworks.
- Experience with ERP implementations, digital transformation, or operating model redesign initiatives.
- Proven track record of leading process improvement and simplification efforts.
- Prior people leadership or demonstrated leadership of project teams and workstreams.

Technical Skills
- Advanced financial modelling and analytics capabilities.
- Advanced Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint skills.
- Experience with business intelligence and visualization tools (Power BI, Tableau, Alteryx, or similar).
- Strong knowledge of ERP platforms and financial reporting systems.
- Strong financial planning and performance management expertise.

- Strategic thinking and business acumen.
- Executive presence and communication skills.
- Ability to influence and drive change.
- Strong stakeholder management and collaboration skills.
- Results-oriented leadership with a continuous improvement mindset.

Job Description:
Manager, Finance Business Partner
Role Overview
The Manager  - Corporate Finance Business Partner is a key member of the Global Services Finance organization within the Global Compensation & Benefits Accounting (Global C&B) process area. This role is responsible for leading Compensation Planning/ Labor Headcount (LHC) Forecasting, and Actuals performance management activities across assigned legal entities for Corporate.
The role serves as a trusted finance partner to Corporate FP&A, Business Unit Finance (BUF), Total Rewards, Benefits, Equity, HR, Payroll, and other cross-functional stakeholders to drive forecasting accuracy, financial transparency, and actionable business insights. The position plays a critical role in translating workforce and compensation data into meaningful financial analyses that support business decisions and enterprise planning cycles.
In addition, the Manager will lead a team supporting both Compensation Planning and Actuals activities while driving continuous improvement, operational excellence, and capability development across the organization.
Key Responsibilities
Finance Business Partnering & Comp/Labor Headcount (LHC) Planning
- Lead the end-to-end labor headcount and compensation forecasting process across assigned legal entities of Corporate.
- Partner with FP&A, Business Unit Finance, Corporate Finance, Total Rewards, Benefits, HR, and Corporate Equity teams to develop accurate workforce and compensation forecasts.
- Drive planning activities for key forecast cycles including Business Plan (BP), June Update (JU), November Update (NU), and Latest Thinking exercises.
- Provide proactive insights on risks, opportunities, trends, and financial impacts related to compensation, benefits, headcount, and workforce costs.
- Challenge assumptions and influence decision-making through data-driven recommendations and scenario analysis.
- Ensure alignment between forecast assumptions, approved positions, headcount movements, and reported financial results.

Financial Planning, Analysis & Reporting
- Own delivery of Compensation Planning/Labor Headcount Forecasting, and Actuals reporting activities for assigned entities.
- Develop executive-level financial presentations, business reviews, dashboard reporting, and analytical commentary for leadership teams.
- Compile and analyze financial and operational metrics, KPIs, and forecast performance indicators.
- Perform variance analysis and explain key drivers impacting compensation, benefits, and workforce-related expenditures.
- Provide clear and concise storytelling of financial results, risks, opportunities, and recommended actions to stakeholders.
- Support quarterly business reviews, leadership discussions, and strategic planning sessions.

Actuals & Financial Close Support
- Ensure accurate accounting and reporting of compensation and workforce-related transactions.
- Support monthly and quarterly close activities through analysis of labor-related expenses, accruals, reconciliations, and reporting.
- Partner with accounting and operational teams to investigate variances and resolve issues impacting financial results.
- Monitor key balance sheet and P&L accounts related to compensation and benefits processes.
- Support internal and external audit requirements, controls execution, and compliance activities.

Leadership & People Management
- Lead and develop a team supporting Compensation Planning and Actuals operations.
- Establish clear goals, priorities, and performance expectations aligned to business objectives.
- Coach and develop team members' technical, analytical, business partnering, and leadership capabilities.
- Foster a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, collaboration, and innovation.
- Promote knowledge sharing, succession planning, and capability building across the organization.

Continuous Improvement & Transformation
- Identify opportunities to enhance forecast accuracy, process efficiency, stakeholder experience, and operational effectiveness.
- Leverage data analytics and visualization tools to improve business insights and decision support.
- Lead process standardization, automation, and transformation initiatives across the planning and reporting landscape.
- Drive adoption of best practices and improve governance over workforce planning and compensation forecasting processes.
- Support broader Global Services and ATR transformation initiatives as required.

Enterprise Leadership
- Champion Johnson & Johnson's Credo and Leadership Imperatives in decision-making and team culture.
- Act as a change leader and advocate for strategic organizational initiatives.
- Build strong relationships across Finance, HR, Payroll, Total Rewards, and other stakeholder groups globally.
- Influence cross-functional teams to achieve business outcomes and enhance organizational effectiveness.

Work Shift : EMEA/Night Shift

Qualifications
Education
- Bachelor's Degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Administration, or related field.
- CPA, CMA, MBA, or equivalent professional qualification preferred.

Experience
- Minimum 5-8 years of progressive experience in Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A), Finance Business Partnering, Workforce Planning, Compensation Planning, or Accounting.
- Prior experience managing teams and leading cross-functional stakeholder engagements.

Position Summary
The AI & Automation Operations Manager will lead the design, implementation, and operationalization of AI-driven workflows, intelligent automation, and observability capabilities across IT Operations and IT Service Management (ITSM). This role is responsible for advancing the organization's journey toward AI-augmented and autonomous operations by leveraging AIOps, Observability tools, Service Now and Generative AI technologies to improve service reliability, reduce operational risk, and accelerate incident resolution.
The role will also provide operational support within the Digital Command Center (DCC), supporting major incident management, executive communications, and continuous service improvement initiatives.

Key Responsibilities
Primary Responsibilities
AI Incident Management
- Design and implement AI-powered workflows for incident detection, triage, categorization, prioritization, and routing.
- Develop AI-assisted root cause analysis, incident enrichment, and predictive incident management capabilities.
- Create intelligent remediation runbooks and automated response workflows.
- Drive reduction of alert noise through event correlation and service intelligence.

AI-Driven Problem & Change Management
- Build workflows that identify recurring issues and proactively generate problem investigations.
- Implement AI-enabled trend analysis, risk scoring, and change impact assessments.
- Support automated generation of knowledge articles, PIR summaries, and operational insights.

AI-Augmented Autonomous Operations
- Develop self-healing and closed-loop remediation capabilities.
- Expand automation across observability tools and ITSM processes.
- Establish governance and operational controls for AI-enabled decision-making and autonomous actions.
- Create dashboards and metrics to demonstrate operational efficiency, reliability improvements, and business value realization.

Secondary Responsibilities
Digital Command Center (DCC) Operations
- Serve as Incident Commander or Major Incident Manager during high-severity incidents.
- Lead cross-functional incident bridges and coordination efforts.
- Develop and deliver executive communications and stakeholder updates.
- Support Incident, Problem, Change, and Knowledge Management governance activities.
- Drive continuous improvement initiatives to enhance operational maturity and resiliency.

Required Qualifications & Skills
Experience
- 5+ years of experience in monitoring, event management, AIOps, observability, production engineering, Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), or IT operations.
- 3+ years of hands-on Observability agentic workflows and Service Now Agent Orchestrator deployments for Operations Center environments.
- Proven experience implementing operational automation, orchestration, or AI-driven solutions.
- Experience supporting enterprise-scale applications and business-critical services.
- Experience leading or supporting major incident management activities.

Technical Skills
- Strong Splunk, Now Assist development and troubleshooting skills.
- Experience with data onboarding, event normalization, MCP service modeling, KPI creation, dashboard development, and analytics.
- Knowledge of Generative AI, AI Agents, Copilot technologies, and AI-assisted workflow design.
- Experience with Python, PowerShell, Bash, REST APIs, or similar automation technologies.
- Experience integrating observability, monitoring, cloud, and ITSM platforms.
- Strong understanding of Incident, Problem, Change, and Knowledge Management processes.
- Experience with ServiceNow or equivalent ITSM platforms.

Leadership & Collaboration
- Excellent communication, documentation, and stakeholder management skills.
- Ability to lead under pressure during critical incidents and service disruptions.
- Strong analytical, problem-solving, and continuous improvement mindset.
- Experience working effectively within global, cross-functional delivery teams.

Preferred Qualifications
- ITIL certification.
- Splunk Power User, Admin, Architect, or ITSI certifications.
- ServiceNow certifications.
- AI, Machine Learning, Data Analytics, or Automation certifications.
- Cloud certifications (AWS, Azure, or GCP).
- Experience implementing autonomous operations or self-healing platforms.

The Data Operations & Access Management Specialist provides support across a broad range of business management, data integrity, access governance, and operational reporting activities. The team ensures data consistency, system hygiene, compliance with internal controls, and timely reporting across multiple business processes.
You will join our Pharmaceutical business and gain exposure to business operations, data governance, reporting, analytics, and cross-functional stakeholder management.
As part of the Global Medical Safety (GMS) organisation, this role also provides visibility into several pharmacovigilance‑adjacent activities, including data quality processes, safety‑related reporting, and interactions with global safety systems. While the position does not require prior pharmacovigilance knowledge, students will gain indirect exposure to PV operations and supporting activities that contribute to patient safety.
This is an office‑based role with global reach, collaborating with colleagues across multiple departments, functions, and countries.
This placement offers a unique opportunity to work at the intersection of data quality, systems access management, operational reporting, and governance, supporting multiple business-critical processes while developing hands-on experience with industry‑standard digital tools (Excel, SharePoint, Power Platform, Power BI).

Main duties and responsibilities:

- Perform data reconciliation and quality checks to ensure consistency, completeness, and accuracy across multiple systems
- Act as a point of contact for data‑related queries and support updates to key data attributes (e.g., cities, states)
- Support periodic access governance cycles, including role‑based access reviews and ad hoc access‑change requests
- Review, prepare, and manage annual access files, including role sorting, identifying relevant approvers, and communicating outcomes
- Coordinate and process bulk onboarding requests, including submission of system access requests and related support items
- Participate in training reconciliation activities, including data review and stakeholder follow‑ups
- Manage and process SharePoint and shared‑drive access requests, ensuring appropriate governance of shared content
- Prepare and deliver recurring operational reports, including LMS vendor staff reporting and product‑specific monthly volume reports
- Support weekly “Out of Cycle” reporting by preparing files, liaising with vendors, and consolidating response comments
- Perform PQC referral timeliness reporting, including vendor coordination and maintaining accurate summary files
- Prepare SUSAR notification reports, consolidate feedback, determine scoring categories, and liaise with business stakeholders
- Conduct quarterly analytics activities, including QLIK data pulls, trend analysis, and updating PowerPoint summaries
- Contribute to workflow trending analysis and associated reporting (where applicable)
- Collaborate with cross‑functional global teams and contribute to onboarding, knowledge transfer, and student cohort engagement activities

Requirements of the role:

- 2 years of degree-level study completed
- A minimum of 2:1 achieved in first year of study
- Preferred degrees: Data, Business, Analytics, Computer Science, Information Systems, STEM, or other relevant fields

Key skills and competencies:

Technical Skills
- Advanced Excel capability, including Pivot Tables, lookups
- SharePoint: ability to manage access, update libraries, and maintain shared structures
- Power Apps & Power Automate (preferred): ability to support or build simple workflows/automation
- Power BI (preferred): ability to support dashboard updates or data modelling
- Strong general digital literacy and ability to learn new systems quickly

Data & Analytical Competencies
- High level of accuracy, attention to detail, and commitment to data integrity
- Ability to manage, interpret, and reconcile data from multiple sources
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills

Business & Professional Skills
- Excellent communication skills, both written and oral
- Ability to prioritise and manage workload independently
- Strong organisational and time‑management skills
- Ability to work cross‑functionally with internal teams globally
- Adaptable and flexible team player
- Self‑motivated and proactive in seeking opportunities to learn
- Comfortable receiving and acting on feedback
- Ability to handle recurring weekly/monthly cycles reliably and consistently

The Director translates platform, product and Supply Chain priorities into integrated supplier, sourcing, contracting, innovation, risk, network and value-creation strategies. The position is accountable across the complete supplier lifecycle, from upstream R&D engagement and supplier selection through contracting, performance management, business continuity, implementation and stabilization.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
1. Platform Leadership & Business Partnership
•  Serve as the senior Procurement leader and single point of accountability for Spine, Sports & CMFT, representing Source in platform, value-stream, financial, innovation and operational governance.
•  Translate business, product and Supply Chain strategies into clear Procurement priorities, roadmaps, resource plans and executive decisions.

2. Procurement Strategy, Financial Performance & Value Creation
•  Own the integrated platform Procurement strategy and contribution to business planning, latest estimates, long-range financial planning and annual targets.
•  Build and govern a credible pipeline for margin expansion, cost competitiveness, productivity and cash flow, supported by defined baselines, Finance validation, milestones and accountable owners.

3. Supplier Strategy, Governance & Performance
•  Own the platform view of the supplier base, including spend, product dependency, ownership, criticality, capability, capacity, performance, risk and growth relevance.
•  Develop supplier segmentation, product-to-supplier mapping, strategic supplier roadmaps and executive engagement plans.

•  Establish measurable performance and development plans, clear escalation paths and disciplined follow-through for critical suppliers.
4. Supply Reliability, Business Continuity & Risk
•  Maintain executive oversight of supplier, component, technology, capacity, financial, geographic, logistics and regulatory risks affecting continuity or growth.
•  Lead the Procurement response to significant disruptions and coordinate mitigation with Planning, Quality, Operations, Technical Operations and Regulatory.

•  Ensure early Procurement engagement in product and technology development, providing supply-market, capability, cost, commercial and risk insights.
•  Oversee supplier identification, due diligence, selection, contracting, qualification and readiness for new-product development, validation, launch and scale-up.

•  Connect unmet business and technical needs with supplier-enabled innovation, automation, materials and manufacturing capabilities.

•  Lead critical RFx processes, market engagements, supplier evaluations and complex negotiations across base business, NPD and transformation programs.

•  Use target cost, should-cost, total cost of ownership and competitive benchmarks to support major decisions.
7. Contracting & Commercial Governance
•  Maintain executive oversight of contract coverage and commercial risk; prioritize agreements based on supplier criticality, spend, exposure and growth dependency.
•  Sponsor strategic supply, development, external-manufacturing and other commercial agreements, amendments and significant claims.
8. Network Strategy, Acquisitions, Transfers & External Manufacturing
•  Lead the Procurement dimension of acquisitions, business integrations, site exits, insourcing and outsourcing decisions, external-manufacturing transitions, product transfers and supplier-network redesign.
•  For acquisitions, lead supplier due diligence, ownership mapping, onboarding, contract review or novation, pricing alignment, risk assessment, systems and master-data readiness, and transition to the future Procurement operating model.
•  For major transfers, lead network assessment, sourcing strategy, competitive RFx, supplier recommendation, contracting, implementation and stabilization.

•  Remain accountable beyond supplier award through supplier readiness, implementation, operational stabilization and long-term value realization.

•  Align permanent and project resources to the highest business priorities, including acquisitions and network transformations.

Finance Leadership Development Program (FLDP) – Japan

Duration: 2.5-year program, followed by permanent position
Start date: January –March 2027

About Johnson & Johnson
At Johnson & Johnson, we use technology and the power of teamwork to discover new ways to prevent and overcome the world’s the most significant healthcare challenges. Our Finance teams leverage data, real-world insights, and creative minds to make life-changing healthcare products and medicines. We're disrupting outdated healthcare ecosystems and infusing them with transformative ideas to help people thrive throughout every stage of their lives. With a reach of more than a billion people every day, there’s no limit to the impact you can make here. Are you ready to reimagine healthcare?
Here, your career breakthroughs will change the future of health, in all the best ways. And you’ll change, too. You’ll be inspired, and you’ll inspire people across the world to change how they care for themselves and those they love. Amplify your impact. Join us!
What is the Finance Leadership Development Program (FLDP)?
The Finance Leadership Development Program (FLDP) is a two-and-a-half-year global program focused on developing future leaders in Finance. To accomplish this mission, participants in the FLDP are placed in positions where they will be challenged, learning core accounting and financial analysis. FLDP participants will have the opportunity to learn and demonstrate leadership skills in areas such as teamwork, risk-taking, and initiative, while demonstrating their core values and adherence to the Johnson & Johnson Credo.
The Job
Most FLDP participants rotate through one 18-month and one 12-month assignment at various ​companies within Johnson & Johnson. During the rotations, FLDP participants will be exposed to various parts of the finance function that could include, but not limited to, Business Unit Finance, Accounting, Tax, Supply Chain and R&D Finance. Each assignment provides an excellent learning experience and an opportunity for FLDP participants to utilize their leadership skills and bring new perspectives for change and process improvement to the J&J companies. Being an FLDP participant exposes you to an expanded network of contacts.
Training
Prior to the program start date of Jan 202 6 , FLDP’s will receive up to six months of “on the job” onboarding .  FLDP offers 5 weeks of in-person training with all global program participants at our J&J World HQ in the US (COVID protocols permitting) during the two-and-a-half-year program to assist in the development of our future leaders. The courses are taught and led by internal J&J management as well as external instructors. In training, the FLDP class enhances their written and oral presentation skills , problem-solving techniques , analytical skills , leadership skills and much more. Overall, training covers areas that are critical to success at Johnson & Johnson and gives the FLDP participants an opportunity to gain the skills necessary to become leaders for tomorrow.​​

If you’re a dynamic and driven individual with a record of achievement and demonstrated leadership potential, we invite you to explore opportunities for accelerated development with FLDP.

FLDP Experience
- Understanding complex and dynamic business environments through interactions with business leaders

- Acquire systems knowledge and technical expertise in widely used financial planning and reporting software (SAP, TM1, Anaplan, etc)

- Master inter-personal and strategic skills through working with cross- functional teams in various businesses and disciplines

- Establish a broad base of knowledge and relationships, including interaction with senior management

- On-the-job coaching and performance feedback from supervisors & coaching from personal mentors, program leaders, and program champions at each company

- Build a solid record of job performance, gain a very broad view of our companies, and discover opportunities across our businesses

- Eligible for a one-time bonus for recognized finance and accounting accreditation

Qualifications
Education
- A minimum of a Bachelor’s degree (preferably in Finance, Accounting & Controlling, Business Administration or Economics). Degrees in fields related to Analytics and Statistics may be considered and/or a clear and demonstrable interest in Finance.

- Sarbanes Oxley experience and CPA, CMA, or other financial certification is preferred. For those without financial certifications, J&J is committed to investing in related training & certification costs to help employees reach these certifications.

Experience & Skills
- 1-3 years of full-time finance or accounting experience is required (not including internships, apprenticeships), MNCs & Big 4 accounting firm experience is preferred.

- Demonstrated technical proficiency (e.g. Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint) and/or prior experience with data analytics & reporting software (e.g. SAP, TM1, Anaplan, Tableau , Power BI ) will be an added advantage.

- Proven ability to work through ambiguity and process design & improvement experience is an asset.

- Demonstrated track-record in influencing business partners with fact-based data and managing change through the use of strong communication skills (verbal, written) including presentations.

DePuy Synthes is recruiting for a  Senior Marketing Manager, Knee Reconstruction , located in Palm Beach Gardens, FL, Warsaw, IN, or Cincinnati, OH to lead the U.S. downstream commercialization strategy for the Depuy Synthes Knee platform.

Position Overview
This Senior Marketing Manager will report to the Director, Knee Reconstruction Marketing, and lead a team accountable for downstream strategy and execution across the DePuy Synthes primary knee portfolio. This leader will own the commercial strategy to accelerate market share growth, drive competitive conversions, deepen surgeon engagement, and strengthen the clinical differentiation of the ATTUNE platform and its underpinning surgical philosophies.

The primary knee implant market is one of the most competitive and clinically consequential spaces in orthopedics. Success requires a leader who can translate deep clinical understanding, market intelligence, and surgeon insights into bold commercial strategies that change surgeon behavior and shift share. This role demands a balance of strategic vision and executional rigor -- setting the direction for the team while ensuring disciplined delivery across multiple concurrent initiatives.

In close partnership with Sales, Upstream Marketing, Medical Affairs, Global Education, R&D, Health Economics, and regional marketing partners, this leader will shape the go-to-market approach for the knee implant portfolio, drive clinical messaging and evidence strategy, and build programs that move surgeons along the adoption continuum from awareness through advocacy. The role will also serve as a key voice in shaping upstream portfolio priorities by ensuring downstream commercial realities and surgeon feedback are reflected in product development, technique evolution, and pipeline planning.

Key Responsibilities
Commercial Strategy & Market Share Growth
- Own and lead the U.S. downstream commercialization strategy for the ATTUNE Knee System, including positioning, messaging, segmentation, competitive response, and market share growth plans.
- Develop and execute strategic plans that drive competitive conversions, expand surgeon adoption of the Solutions in Motion philosophy, and accelerate penetration of the Kinematic Restoration surgical approach across target segments.
- Define and prioritize target surgeon segments based on procedural volume, competitive usage, clinical philosophy alignment, and conversion potential; build tailored engagement strategies for each segment.
- Establish pricing and contracting strategy inputs in partnership with Sales Operations and Commercial Excellence to optimize portfolio value capture.
- Set annual and quarterly commercial objectives, allocate resources against highest-impact opportunities, and manage the marketing budget to deliver ROI.

Clinical Messaging & Evidence Strategy
- Lead the development of differentiated clinical value messaging for the ATTUNE platform, grounded in biomechanical evidence, clinical outcomes data, and the Kinematic Restoration surgical rationale.
- Partner with Medical Affairs and Health Economics to build and deploy the clinical evidence strategy, including publication planning support, evidence compendium development, and health economic value propositions.
- Translate complex biomechanical and clinical concepts into compelling, surgeon-relevant narratives that resonate across different adopter profiles -- from early innovators to pragmatic majority.
- Ensure all clinical messaging is defensible, compliant, and competitively differentiated; oversee regulatory and legal review processes for the team's output.

Go-to-Market Planning & Launch Excellence
- Lead go-to-market planning for new implant configurations, instrument innovations, technique evolutions, and platform enhancements, ensuring field readiness and clear success metrics.
- Define launch strategy including phased rollout plans, early adopter identification, training requirements, field communications, and post-launch performance tracking.
- Coordinate cross-functional launch readiness across Sales, Upstream Marketing, Global Education, Supply Chain, and Sales Operations to ensure seamless commercial execution.
- Conduct post-launch reviews to capture learnings and continuously improve launch processes.

Surgeon Education, Engagement & Advocacy
- Shape the surgeon education and engagement strategy in partnership with Global Education, including cadaver labs, technique training programs, peer-to-peer forums, fellowship engagement, and visiting surgeon programs.
- Build and manage key opinion leader (KOL) relationships and surgeon advisory boards that inform strategy, validate messaging, and amplify clinical advocacy.
- Lead platform presence and engagement strategy at major society meetings including AAOS, AAHKS, and relevant regional and subspecialty conferences.
- Develop surgeon advocacy programs that convert satisfied users into active champions who drive peer influence and referral in partnership with the DS Surgeon Alliance team.

Competitive Intelligence & Market Insights
- Own the competitive intelligence function for the primary knee implant market; monitor competitive launches, clinical publications, messaging shifts, pricing dynamics, and market share trends.
- Translate competitive and market insights into actionable strategic recommendations, including defensive positioning, proactive response plans, and opportunity identification.
- Lead voice-of-customer research programs to continuously refine understanding of surgeon needs, adoption barriers, decision drivers, and satisfaction across the ATTUNE installed base.
- Deliver regular market and performance briefings to the Director and senior leadership with clear strategic implications and recommended actions.

Field Enablement & Sales Partnership
- Partner with Sales leadership to ensure the field organization is equipped with the tools, training, messaging, and competitive resources needed to win in the market.
- Develop and maintain a comprehensive field enablement toolkit including selling guides, competitive battle cards, objection handlers, account targeting resources, and customer engagement playbooks.
- Support key account strategy and high-value conversion opportunities in partnership with regional sales leaders and field marketing teams.
- Establish feedback loops with the field to continuously refine commercial programs based on real-world effectiveness and surgeon response.

Team Leadership & Development
- Lead, coach, and develop a team of marketing managers and associate marketing managers; set clear expectations, provide regular feedback, and foster a culture of accountability, curiosity, and continuous improvement.
- Set team priorities and manage workload allocation to ensure disciplined execution across multiple concurrent initiatives without sacrificing strategic focus.
- Build team capabilities in clinical marketing, competitive strategy, evidence-based messaging, and cross-functional leadership.
- Attract and retain top talent; support career development and succession planning within the team.

Upstream Partnership & Portfolio Influence
- Partner with R&D and upstream marketing to ensure downstream commercial requirements, surgeon feedback, and market insights are reflected in portfolio priorities, product design, technique development, and pipeline planning.
- Provide input on user experience, workflow design, and instrumentation based on field and surgeon feedback.

- Proven ability to develop and execute commercial strategies that drive measurable market share growth and competitive conversion.
- Strong analytical skills with experience in business performance reporting, market analytics, and financial modeling.
- Exceptional communication and presentation skills with the ability to influence senior leadership, cross-functional partners, and surgeon customers.

This Marketing Manager will report to the Senior Marketing Manager, Knee Reconstruction Marketing, and serve as a critical execution leader responsible for independently owning and delivering key marketing workstreams across the DePuy Synthes primary knee implant portfolio. This individual will manage projects end-to-end, develop marketing programs with increasing strategic input, and may provide day-to-day guidance to associate-level team members.
This role sits at the inflection point between executional support and strategic ownership. The Marketing Manager is expected to operate with a high degree of independence -- taking a brief or strategic direction from senior leadership and translating it into fully developed plans, programs, and deliverables without heavy oversight. The role requires someone who can think critically about the "why" behind the work, not just the "what," and who is beginning to develop a point of view on commercial strategy informed by data, competitive dynamics, and surgeon insights.
In partnership with Sales, Upstream Marketing, Medical Affairs, Global Education, R&D, and Sales Operations, this individual will lead the execution of clinical messaging programs, campaign development, launch workstreams, surgeon education initiatives, and competitive response tactics that drive market share growth and deepen surgeon engagement with the ATTUNE platform.

Key Responsibilities
Clinical Messaging & Program Development
- Own the development of clinical marketing materials for the ATTUNE Knee System, including surgeon-facing collateral, evidence summaries, technique differentiation content, and value messaging aligned to the Solutions in Motion philosophy and Kinematic Restoration approach.
- Lead the translation of clinical data, biomechanical evidence, and surgical technique differentiators into compelling, segment-specific messaging -- moving beyond content creation to strategic narrative development.
- Manage the end-to-end content development process including agency briefing, creative direction, stakeholder input, and regulatory/legal/medical affairs review cycles.
- Identify messaging gaps and proactively recommend new content or program concepts based on field feedback, competitive shifts, and market trends.

Campaign Ownership & Field Enablement
- Own the planning, development, and execution of integrated marketing campaigns that drive surgeon awareness, trial, adoption, and advocacy for the ATTUNE platform across priority segments.
- Develop and refine field enablement tools including selling guides, competitive battle cards, objection handlers, account targeting resources, and customer engagement playbooks.
- Partner with Marketing Services and Sales to ensure campaigns and tools are relevant, actionable, and aligned to regional priorities and account-level opportunities.
- Track campaign performance against defined KPIs, analyze results, and iterate on tactics to improve effectiveness over time.

Launch Execution & Readiness
- Lead assigned workstreams within go-to-market launches for new implant configurations, instrument updates, technique evolutions, and platform enhancements.
- Develop launch deliverables including field training materials, sales communications, customer-facing content, and post-launch tracking frameworks.
- Coordinate cross-functional inputs and dependencies across Sales, Global Education, Supply Chain, and Sales Operations to ensure on-time readiness.
- Own launch milestone tracking for assigned workstreams and escalate risks with recommended solutions.

Surgeon Education & Engagement
- Lead the planning and execution of assigned surgeon education programs, including cadaver labs, product demonstrations, peer-to-peer events, and fellowship engagement initiatives.
- Develop educational content that articulates the clinical rationale behind Kinematic Restoration and the biomechanical advantages of the ATTUNE platform for target surgeon audiences.
- Support key opinion leader (KOL) engagements and surgeon advisory boards, including agenda development, discussion facilitation support, and insight capture and synthesis.
- Manage assigned society meeting deliverables, including booth content, presentation materials, and on-site engagement tactics.

Competitive Intelligence & Market Analysis
- Conduct in-depth competitive analysis on primary knee implant competitors, including product positioning, clinical evidence claims, messaging strategies, and market share dynamics.
- Develop competitive response recommendations and proactively identify opportunities to sharpen ATTUNE differentiation based on competitive vulnerabilities.
- Lead assigned voice-of-customer research initiatives, synthesize findings, and present actionable insights to the senior marketing team.
- Build and maintain market and performance dashboards; deliver regular business reviews with analysis that connects data to strategic implications.

Cross-Functional Partnership & Coordination
- Serve as a primary marketing point of contact for assigned cross-functional workstreams, building productive relationships with Sales, Upstream Marketing, Medical Affairs, Global Education, R&D, and Supply Chain.
- Provide downstream market perspective and surgeon feedback into upstream discussions on product development, technique design, and portfolio planning.

Johnson & Johnson is currently recruiting for a Director, Regulatory Compliance- RAD! This position will be located in Santa Clara, CA.
Position Summary:
The Director, Regulatory Compliance – RAD provides independent, strategic regulatory compliance oversight for the RAD business, with particular emphasis on robotics-enabled medical technology, software and software-enabled devices, connected-device and product-cybersecurity compliance, and Health Authority/Notified Body inspection readiness and management.
The Director interprets current and emerging regulatory requirements, standards, and regulator expectations; translates them into risk-based compliance strategies; and provides independent advice, challenge, escalation, and oversight across the product and quality-system lifecycle. The role partners with Quality, Regulatory Affairs, R&D/Engineering, Software, Product Cybersecurity, Manufacturing/Operations, Clinical, Legal, Supply Chain, and business leadership to identify, assess, communicate, escalate, and oversee mitigation of material quality and regulatory-compliance risks.
The Director leads inspection-readiness strategy and coordinates significant Health Authority, MDSAP, and Notified Body inspection-management activities for the assigned RAD scope. The role provides oversight of inspection responses, remediation, internal-audit follow-up, and effectiveness monitoring, and may act as delegate to the Senior Director, Regulatory Compliance when formally assigned.
Key Responsibilities:
- Develops and implements the RAD regulatory-compliance strategy for assigned products, sites, legal manufacturers, and quality-system processes, aligned with MedTech Quality & Compliance and JJRC strategies.

- Provides independent compliance advice, challenge, and escalation on significant product, software, cybersecurity, quality-system, and inspection risks; ensures that risk decisions, ownership, rationale, and required actions are transparent and appropriately governed.

- Monitors the external regulatory environment for requirements and enforcement trends affecting robotics, connected devices, device software, cybersecurity, AI-enabled functionality where applicable, quality systems, and inspections; assesses business impact and drives timely implementation plans.

- Represents RAD Regulatory Compliance in designated risk-management boards, quality-review boards, management reviews, product-development governance, compliance councils, and leadership forums; escalates material risks to the Senior Director and appropriate governance bodies.

- Provides compliance oversight across the lifecycle of robotics-enabled and computer-assisted medical-device systems , including system integration, hardware/software interfaces, usability and training controls, safety/performance evidence, postmarket signals, and significant product or process changes.

- Challenges and evaluates the adequacy of software compliance controls for embedded software, device software functions, software accessories, cloud or remote functionality, interoperability, and modular software, including lifecycle planning, requirements, architecture, verification, validation, release, maintenance, configuration management, and change control.

- Assesses whether software functions and changes are appropriately governed under applicable regional requirements, including FDA device-software expectations and EU MDR software qualification/classification, and ensures material compliance gaps are escalated and remediated.

- Provides independent compliance oversight for AI-enabled functionality, when applicable , including lifecycle risk controls and predetermined change-control plans or analogous regulatory mechanisms.

- Provides independent regulatory-compliance oversight of the product-cybersecurity quality system for software-enabled and connected RAD products, while preserving the legal manufacturer’s accountability for product safety, effectiveness, design controls, and residual-risk decisions.

- Owns the regulatory-compliance inspection-readiness framework for assigned RAD sites and functions, including risk-based readiness assessments, mock inspections, management and SME preparedness, evidence availability, and timely remediation of identified gaps.

- Leads or coordinates significant Health Authority, MDSAP, and Notified Body inspections within assigned scope, including inspection strategy, escalation, cross-site coordination, and alignment with Quality, Regulatory Affairs, Legal, Operations, and business leadership.

- Provides independent review and oversight of inspection communications and responses , including observation interpretation, investigation depth, risk assessment, corrective and preventive actions, commitments, milestones, and evidence of implementation and effectiveness.

- Maintains oversight of inspection commitments through closure and uses inspection, audit, complaint, CAPA, postmarket, cybersecurity, and compliance trend data to identify systemic or recurring risk.

- Oversees a robust, risk-based, closed-loop internal-audit program for the assigned scope and ensures audit results inform compliance risk assessment and inspection readiness.

- Provides compliance oversight of significant remediation programs, special investigations, post-acquisition assessments, and field-action follow-up , including adequate scope, governance, escalation, resources, and effectiveness.

- Uses compliance data and regulatory intelligence to identify trends, prioritize risk reduction, and communicate actionable insights to RAD and JJRC leadership.

- Supports due diligence, acquisitions, integrations, divestitures, and new-product introductions , with particular attention to robotics, software, cybersecurity, technical documentation, and inspection-readiness risks.

- Builds effective relationships across global, regional, site, and functional teams and influences decisions where the role does not have direct authority.

- Develops organizational capability in emerging technology-compliance areas, including robotics, software, connected devices, cybersecurity, digital health, and inspection management.

- Coaches and develops direct reports and matrix team members where applicable and ensures resources are aligned to assigned compliance priorities.

Overview of the Role

Johnson & Johnson is seeking a Manager, Procurement CCPM, to support Capital Construction, Project Management & Capital Equipment expenditure in Schaffhausen, Switzerland. This is a site-based role, and the Schaffhausen site is the only location for this posting. The role provides procurement leadership across sourcing, supplier management, contract execution, value delivery, and operational excellence for Capital Construction and Project Management and Capital Equipment related CAPEX categories supporting site investment projects.
J&J continues to invest significant capital to build, expand, retrofit, and optimize assets across manufacturing sites, laboratories, distribution, and offices. This role helps enable speed-to-market, supply chain excellence, and employee experience through market-leading safety, productivity, cost, and technology/innovation outcomes, supported by strategic supplier partnerships in Architecture, Engineering, Construction & Project Management, Commissioning, Qualification, Project Safety and Controls.

Collaboration and Delivery

The Manager, Procurement CCPM will work closely with Engineering & Property Services (E&PS) and Global Engineering Technology (GET), particularly Engineering Design, Project Delivery, Construction, and site engineering teams. The role also partners with suppliers providing Architectural & Engineering (A&E), Construction Management (CM), Automation, and Commissioning & Qualification (C&Q) services, as well as with local and regional business stakeholders, to support successful project delivery.

Organisational Context

The CCPM and CE categories sit within the Capital, Construction & Facilities Services family and supports Johnson & Johnson’s Enterprise Procurement and Supply Chain Services Procurement priorities. The role acts as a strategic procurement partner to site leadership, Plant/Facility Engineering, Technical Services, Quality, Finance, EHS, and Procurement leadership.

·         Category leadership and sourcing: Implement and support category strategies for Capital Construction, Capital Equipment  and related CAPEX categories, including negotiated agreements, preferred suppliers, value engineering, sourcing execution, contract implementation, compliance, and target delivery.
